title: Star wreath motif
subtitle: Five five-pointed stars joined in a ring, 25 cm across
excerpt: The star wreath links five crochet stars at adjacent points into a circular arrangement, leaving a pentagonal opening at the centre. Each star is a five-pointed piece worked from a magic ring with treble spokes and chain tip loops. The finished wreath at 25 cm in DK cotton works as a door wreath, Christmas wall hanging, and table centrepiece.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 4 (1889), star and wreath motif chapter (Internet Archive). Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886), crochet star and joined motif construction.

chartDefinition.title: Star wreath motif
chartDefinition.caption: Five individual five-pointed stars joined at adjacent tips. Each star: magic ring, 5 treble spokes with ch-5 tip loops. Joining: chain-join between tip loops of adjacent stars.

glossaryTerms.definition: Multiple trebles worked into the same space and drawn together at the top. Each of the five star spokes is a treble cluster from the magic ring centre.

content.text: Each star in the wreath has five
treble cluster

spokes from a magic ring, with a ch-5 point at the end of each spoke tipped with a dc. Stars 2 through 5 replace two of their five tip dc stitches with chain joins into the adjacent star, closing the wreath. The first star is complete and free; star 5 joins to both stars 4 and 1 to close the ring.

attrs.title: Materials for one wreath
attrs.body: About 30 g of DK cotton for all five stars. A 4 mm hook. Tapestry needle. Scissors. Optional: hanging ring and ribbon.

content.text: Gauge
Each individual star measures 10 cm across. The joined wreath measures 25 cm across in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook.
Stitches used
chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st), magic ring (MR) — UK and US shared.
double crochet (dc) — UK; US "single crochet".
treble cluster (3tr-cl) — three trebles drawn together.
Pattern
Star 1 — complete and free

Form a magic ring. Ch 3 (counts as first tr of first cluster). Work 2 more tr into ring, draw together (first 3tr-cl). *Ch 2. 3tr-cl into ring.* Repeat 3 more times. Ch 2. Sl st to top of first cluster. (5 clusters, 5 ch-2 spaces.) For each of the 5 points: *Sl st into ch-2 sp. Ch 5. Dc into 2nd ch from hook (point tip). Ch 3. Sl st back into the ch-2 sp.* Repeat 4 more times. Fasten off.
Stars 2 through 4 — joined on 2 points

Work the centre clusters as for star 1. For 3 free points, work as star 1. For the 2 joined points: Ch 5. Ch 3. Sl st into the corresponding tip of the adjacent star. Ch 3. Sl st back to the ch-2 space. This links the tip without a separate dc point — the adjacent star's dc serves as the shared tip.
Star 5 — closing the wreath
Work 2 free points and 2 joined points to stars 4 and 1. Check placement before working the closing joins.

definition.title: Star wreath motif
definition.caption: Five stars in a ring. Each star: 5 treble clusters from magic ring, ch-5/dc tips. Join stars at two adjacent tips each.

content.text: Finishing
Weave in all ends. Attach a hanging loop of ribbon or a curtain ring to one of the star outer tips. Block each star flat with T-pins if needed.
Care
Handwash in cool water. Re-pin and block to dry. The join points are secure but benefit from a light steam if the stars have shifted.
What to try next

The joined snowflake wreath (crochet-snowflake-joined) uses the same six-unit joined arrangement with snowflake units instead of stars. The moon-star motif (crochet-themed-moon-star) combines the star with a crescent for a celestial-themed piece.
